summary: Company recovery / same-company detection (C6). Backend: the existing test_company_recovery.py and test_company_created_once.py pass 10/10. I added test_company_recovery_extra.py with 11 tests: 10 pass and 1 fails, and the failure is a real race condition. Verified working: recovery-code format XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX (no 0/O/1/I); same name+phone+address with a new key returns 409 company_exists; a different address creates a new company; precheck returns true/false, and 401 with a bad credential; recover returns 404 for a wrong code, 200 for the right code typed in lower case with spaces, keeps the same company_id with a new installation_id, the old PC gets 403 and retries are idempotent; recover returns 401 for a bad credential and 422 for a too-short code; using a key that belongs to another active company returns 409; signed recovery-code and company endpoints work and return 401 unsigned; a blank company name returns 422; admin lookup works by name and by id, and returns 401 with no header or a wrong one; legacy /activate and /installation/register give the same company_id, also concurrently; setup recover verify/backups/restore-folder return 409. Office GET /api/recovery-code returns 403 for sales and 503 'Read recovery code failed: Not Found' for the owner, which is expected because the production CP is not deployed yet. Frontend: the owner sees the recovery-code card on Settings > Company Profile in the expected error state, and Try again shows loading then the error again. A sales user does not see the card.

critical.issue: Race condition creates duplicate companies. When 6 NEW keys register the same name+phone+address at the same time, 2 companies are created ([409,200,409,200,409,409]); this happened in 2 of 3 runs. The advisory lock is keyed on the public key, so different keys never wait for each other, and companies.match_key has only a non-unique index. The user explicitly asked for a DB rule preventing duplicates.

minor.issue: Bypasses an admin revoke. After POST /installations/{id}/revoke, recovering with the company's code on a new key returns 200 with a new ACTIVE installation and entitlement. The code also forces license_row.status='ACTIVE', so a suspended or revoked license is silently reactivated. Only Company.status is checked.

No rate limiting. The bootstrap credential ships inside Office, so anyone can check whether a company exists by name+phone+address, and can guess recovery codes without limit. The codes carry 100 bits of entropy, so guessing is low risk, but throttling or audit is advisable.
The raw CP error reaches the user: 'Read recovery code failed: Not Found.' The card then says 'You can also view it later in Admin → Settings → Company' even when the user is already on that page.

issues: The recovery card error text is a technical message ('Read recovery code failed: Not Found'). Show a friendly message instead, such as 'Couldn't reach RoofSpan right now'.
The text 'view it later in Admin → Settings → Company' is redundant on the Settings page itself. Hide it there, for example via a prop.

action_items: Make company dedupe race-safe. Add a partial UNIQUE index on companies(match_key) WHERE status='ACTIVE' AND match_key IS NOT NULL, plus an Alembic migration that handles existing duplicates. Also take an advisory lock on match_key in register, and catch the IntegrityError and turn it into 409 company_exists.

In /installation/recover: refuse (403) when the company's license or installations were admin-REVOKED or the subscription is SUSPENDED, rather than force-setting license status to ACTIVE. At minimum, only change the license's installation_id.
Consider rate limiting or audit logging on /installation/precheck and /installation/recover.
Make the RecoveryCodeCard error text friendly, and hide the 'view it later in Settings' hint when the card is shown inside Settings.

Update /app/memory/test_credentials.md: sales@example.com / SalesRS#2026 does NOT exist in the users table (it is missing from the DB, probably because a backup was restored). sales_bk@example.com / SalesBk#2026 works.
critical_code_review_comments: installation_router.register_installation: the match_key check and the company insert are not protected against concurrent first registrations with different keys. There is no DB unique constraint on match_key.
installation_router.recover_installation sets license_row.status='ACTIVE' unconditionally. That reactivates licenses an operator disabled.
installation_company / installation_recovery_code rely on service.audit() to commit. That works, but the commit is implicit and fragile: if the audit call moves, the change silently isn't saved.
admin_company_lookup generates and persists a recovery code as a side effect of a GET for pre-C6 companies. This is acceptable but worth documenting.
test_credentials: Owner pjacobsen@asgardsolution.io / RoofSpan#Owner2026 works. sales@example.com / SalesRS#2026 does NOT exist (401); sales_bk@example.com / SalesBk#2026 was used instead.
seed_data_creation: The tests created many TEST 'Acme Roofing <hex>' companies and installations in the Control Plane Postgres DB (no delete API exists). One was admin-revoked during the revoke test. No Office data was changed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=... python -m pytest tests/test_company_recovery*.py tests/test_company_created_once.py -p no:cacheprovider. test_concurrent_same_company_different_keys_creates_one is flaky until match_key becomes unique; it fails about 2 times in 3. The Setup restore UI can't be tested because users exist. The Office talks to production cp.roofspan.io, so the owner card shows the error state.
rca of the issue: Duplicate companies: register serializes on pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(public_key)). Two different new PCs hold different locks, both SELECT match_key and find nothing, and both INSERT a Company. ix_companies_match_key is non-unique, so the DB accepts both rows. Fix: add a unique partial index on match_key plus a match_key advisory lock, and map the IntegrityError to 409.
